binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with an instance asserting that μ is a probability measure.
An arbitrary real-valued function X : Ω → ℝ.
In the first conjunct, an arbitrary exponent p in the extended nonnegative reals ENNReal.
hypotheses: The measure μ is a probability measure.
For the first identity, p is not zero.
For the first identity, p is not top (infinity).
conclusions: For every finite positive p, eLpNorm X p μ equals (∫⁻ ω, enorm(X(ω))^(p.toReal) ∂μ)^(1 / p.toReal), with both powers interpreted as ENNReal.rpow.
At p = top, eLpNorm X top μ equals eLpNormEssSup X μ, the μ-essential supremum of the pointwise extended norm of X.
mathematical_definitions: ENNReal is [0,∞], the nonnegative reals with an added infinity element; the equalities are ENNReal-valued.
For finite p, p.toReal is its ordinary nonnegative real value, and the guards p ≠ 0 and p ≠ top make it a positive real exponent.
The pointwise quantity enorm(X(ω)) is the usual norm |X(ω)| of a real number, represented in ENNReal.
lintegral is the ENNReal-valued lower Lebesgue integral, written ∫⁻, so it can return infinity.
eLpNorm is defined by cases: zero at exponent 0, eLpNormEssSup at exponent top, and eLpNorm' otherwise.
eLpNormEssSup X μ is essSup (ω ↦ enorm(X(ω))) μ.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On every measurable space, for every probability measure μ and every function X from that space to the real numbers, two statements hold simultaneously: for every extended-nonnegative-real exponent p other than 0 and infinity, the extended Lp seminorm of X is the reciprocal-p power of the lower Lebesgue integral of |X| to the p power; and at exponent infinity, the extended Lp seminorm is the μ-essential supremum of |X|.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure is restricted to a probability measure; the proposition does not state the identities for arbitrary measures.
No measurability, almost-everywhere strong measurability, or integrability hypothesis is imposed on X; X is an arbitrary function Ω → ℝ.
The finite-exponent clause covers every p with 0 < p < infinity, including 0 < p < 1; it is not restricted to the norm range p ≥ 1.
All norm and integral values lie in ENNReal, so the proposition permits infinite values and asserts no finiteness of the integral or eLpNorm.
The hypotheses p ≠ 0 and p ≠ top are nested implications; only exponents satisfying both conditions are constrained by the first clause.
The p = 0 behavior of eLpNorm is not asserted as a conclusion, because p = 0 is excluded from the first clause and the second clause concerns only top.
The top-exponent equality directly matches the top branch displayed in the supplied definition of eLpNorm and therefore carries no additional side condition on X.
The probability-measure condition is an instance argument: the proposition applies only when such evidence for μ is available.
ambiguities: The supplied one-level body of lintegral is an opaque wrapper projection, so its detailed construction and conventions cannot be reconstructed from the dossier beyond its ENNReal-valued integral role.

The nonexceptional helper eLpNorm' appears only inside the supplied body of eLpNorm and is not itself defined in the dependency inventory; the explicit equality in the target is nevertheless unambiguous because its right-hand side is fully elaborated.
